newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati Bell approves shareholder plan.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati Bell approves shareholder plan.

text.p: Cincinnati Bell Inc said Monday its board of directors adopted a shareholder rights plan, updating a similar plan that expired last November.
The company said the new plan, like its predecessor, is to deter coercive or unfair takeover tactics in the event of an unsolicited acquisition proposal.

It will give the board greater flexibility to protect shareowner interests and could prevent an acquirer from gaining control of Cincinnati Bell without offering fair treatment to all shareowners, it said.

"The Board is not aware of any current circumstances that would invoke provisions of the rights plan," it said. "No shareowner owns 15 percent or has indicated intentions to acquire 15 percent of Cincinnati Bell's shares."
In approving the plan, which takes effect May 2, the board also declared a dividend of one preferred-share purchase right for each outstanding Cincinnati Bell common share owned on May 2, it said.
Cincinnati Bell helps communications companies compete through advanced billing, customer information and marketing solutions. It also operates as a communications services in Cincinnati.
